note: Week of 2026-10-12 build. Run fired on schedule Sunday 10/11 ~9:00pm CT; entries are recorded at official SIP regular-session closes of Friday 2026-10-09 (connected brokerage market-data feed) and open Monday 10/12. Monday is Columbus Day: US stock markets are OPEN (bond market closed), so the week starts as normal. PRIOR WEEK (10/5-10/9) realized +301.41 (+0.40%), 6 of 10 names green: MPC +7.74% (+490.50) and VLO +6.76% (+439.20) led on Houthi-Saudi escalation; PWR +4.34%, AMZN +4.34%, TSLA +3.27%, GEV +1.62%. Losses: TER -10.32% (-695.40) and LRCX -8.24% (-544.35) as semi-equipment gave back the prior week's run; DAL -2.28% (Q3 miss, trimmed FY outlook); NVDA -2.00%. Capital rolled forward to $74,963.06. New book: 11 names, $67,348.72 deployed (89.8%), cash $7,614.34. Carried forward: PWR, AMZN, MPC, VLO. Exited all semis (NVDA, TER, LRCX), TSLA, DAL, and GEV (momentum slowing, earnings 10/21; dropped to keep cash in the 8-15% band). EARNINGS INSIDE THE WINDOW: UNH Tue 10/13 before the open (binary; sized 6.6%). Other dated events: big-bank earnings Tue-Wed (JPM, GS, C, WFC, then BAC, MS); September CPI Wed 10/14 (consensus ~3.6% y/y headline) plus Beige Book; ASML Wed, TSMC Thu; PPI/retail sales later in the week. Macro: S&P 500 7,811.54 (+1.2% w/w) near a record, Nasdaq 4th straight weekly gain; 10-year ~5.24% after a 24-year high of ~5.37% Wednesday; Brent ~$104.5, WTI ~$93; gold ~$4,220; VIX ~14.8; S&P futures +0.1-0.3% Sunday evening. Themes: managed-care re-rate on 2027 MA star ratings (HUM, UNH), hyperscaler nuclear/power deals (CEG, PWR, AMZN), SpaceX spectrum deal re-rating tower REITs (CCI, AMT), PLTR double upgrade to new highs, refiners/gold as the geopolitical hedge (MPC, VLO, AEM). Zero semis, zero financials this week.

positions.name: Humana
positions.catalyst: Closed Friday 10/9 at $431.87, +11.6% on the day on 5.0M shares (2.6x the 2-week average) after CMS 2027 Medicare Advantage star ratings put ~95% of Humana members in 4+ star plans vs 20% for 2026 - far above JPM's 60-70% expectation (Fierce Healthcare called Humana the clear winner). Baird upgraded to Outperform and lifted its PT to $596 from $390. New 52-week high ($456.50 intraday); the stock has nearly tripled off the $163 March low.
positions.risks: Gapped to $450 and faded to $431.87, so the open already contains a lot; bonus payments arrive in 2028, not 2027; 2026 EPS guide only >= $9. UNH reports Tue 10/13 and its tone sets the group.
positions.driver: The cleanest fresh catalyst in the market - a fundamental re-rate with an upgrade and 2.6x volume.

positions.name: UnitedHealth Group
positions.catalyst: Closed Friday 10/9 at $379.30, +2.0% on the week and +1.6% Friday in sympathy with Humana's star-ratings beat (Seeking Alpha: UNH rose on the Medicare Star Ratings update). Reports Q3 Tue 10/13 before the open (EPS est. $4.14) - the first big managed-care print after the 2027 stars data, and an opportunity to reset guidance with the sector re-rating.
positions.risks: Binary earnings Tuesday - sized smallest (6.6%). Still 18% below its $461.62 July high; medical-cost trend commentary can swing the stock several percent either way.
positions.driver: Managed-care rotation leader that gets its own catalyst inside the window.

positions.name: Constellation Energy
positions.catalyst: Closed Friday 10/9 at $298.07, +15.8% on the week (from $257.49) on ~2x average volume. Monday 10/6 it jumped 12-14% on new 20-year hyperscaler nuclear deals: an Amazon contract backing >$3B and a ~190 MW uprate at Calvert Cliffs, with reports also citing a Google agreement covering uprates at 11 units (>$4.3B). Contracted, long-dated AI-power cash flows are the market's favorite utility story.
positions.risks: Already ran $257 -> $310 intraday; FERC delayed PJM's Reliability Backstop plan to 2027 (regulatory overhang); BMO trimmed its PT to $350. 10-year at ~5.24% pressures utility multiples; CPI Wed is the macro risk.
positions.driver: Fresh multi-billion hyperscaler deals plus a breakout week on double volume.

positions.name: Quanta Services
positions.catalyst: Carried forward after +4.34% last week; closed Friday 10/9 at $705.94, a fourth straight higher weekly close and out of the $610-$655 September range. Grid/transmission buildout for AI data centers (the same theme as CEG's uprates) is the most persistent non-semi capex trade; Friday's close was near the high of the day.
positions.risks: 80x trailing earnings; still 10% below the $788.75 May high, so there is overhead supply. Q3 earnings late October are outside the window. Correlated with CEG.
positions.driver: Breakout with follow-through - let the winner run another week.

positions.name: Crown Castle
positions.catalyst: Closed Friday 10/9 at $79.64, +15.6% on the day on 14.4M shares (3.1x average) - the biggest gainer in the S&P 500 - after SpaceX agreed to buy ~$8B of nationwide 800 MHz low-band spectrum from Grain Management for Starlink Mobile. Bernstein said the deal keeps the tower-leasing option 'very much alive', estimating a full buildout needs 30k-120k tower sites vs only 1.2k-2k new towers permitted per year. Bounced off a 52-week low set Monday 10/5 ($65.32).
positions.risks: No SpaceX tower lease is signed and FCC approval is pending - the move is a hypothesis; part is short covering in a stock down ~22% YTD. One-day gaps this size can partially fill. Rate-sensitive REIT with the 10-year at 5.24%.
positions.driver: Highest-volume fresh catalyst of the week, off a 52-week low with room to run.

positions.name: American Tower
positions.catalyst: Closed Friday 10/9 at $182.24, +9.3% on the day on 8.5M shares (2.5x average) and +12.4% on the week, on the same SpaceX spectrum catalyst; the largest and most liquid tower REIT with the biggest US macro-tower footprint for any new direct-to-cell carrier. Still 7% below the $196.08 June high.
positions.risks: Same unsigned-tenant hypothesis as CCI (paired exposure, so both are sized below 8%); carriers - AMT's actual tenants - sold off 6-13% on fears of a new competitor. Rate-sensitive.
positions.driver: Higher-quality second leg of the tower re-rate.

positions.name: Palantir Technologies
positions.catalyst: Closed Friday 10/9 at $209.05, a new 52-week/all-time closing high, +10.8% on the week (from $188.75) and +5.2% Friday on 37.6M shares (1.7x average). Two upgrades in two days: Goldman Sachs to Buy with a $230 PT on 10/8 (sovereign-AI thesis) and Barclays to Overweight/strong-buy on 10/9. The stock rose on 10/8 even as the market fell.
positions.risks: 178x earnings and RSI ~70 - stretched; Zacks downgraded to Hold and Schwab clients were net sellers. High-beta software is exposed to a hot CPI print Wednesday. Earnings 11/2 are outside the window.
positions.driver: Double-upgrade breakout to new highs - pure momentum + news.

positions.name: Amazon
positions.catalyst: Carried forward after +4.34% last week; closed Friday 10/9 at $262.43, its best close since mid-September, through Prime Big Deal Days (10/6-10/7) and a new 20-year nuclear power deal with Constellation that secures AWS capacity. Mega-caps (MAGS +1% Friday) led the rebound from Thursday's tech dip.
positions.risks: Still 9% below the $287.20 August high; Q3 report late October is outside the window; rate-sensitive mega-cap multiple.
positions.driver: Mega-cap with improving relative strength and an AWS power catalyst.

positions.name: Marathon Petroleum
positions.catalyst: Carried forward after +7.74% last week; closed Friday 10/9 at $455.03 after a new all-time high of $470.00 intraday. Product markets stay tight as Houthi strikes on Saudi Arabia escalate (Aramco site near Riyadh hit 10/3; Saturday's airport attack killed 12) with Brent ~$104.5 and WTI ~$93 to end the week.
positions.risks: Trump's Russia diesel-supply deal (announced 10/8) is a direct headwind for cracks; Friday reversed from $470 to $455. Stock is up ~180% from the December low - very extended.
positions.driver: Strongest-trending energy name; geopolitical hedge for the book.

positions.name: Valero Energy
positions.catalyst: Carried forward after +6.76% last week; closed Friday 10/9 at $433.75 after a new 52-week high of $449.77 intraday on 3.35M shares (1.3x average). Same tight-product backdrop as MPC: escalating Houthi attacks on Saudi energy infrastructure and Brent >$100.
positions.risks: Same diesel-deal headwind and the same intraday reversal as MPC; pairs with MPC so energy is ~17% of the book. Q3 earnings ~10/22 are outside the window.
positions.driver: Second refiner leg with confirmed volume.

positions.name: Agnico Eagle Mines
positions.catalyst: Closed Friday 10/9 at $189.02, +2.9% on the week, as gold rose 1.5% Friday to ~$4,220/oz on Middle East escalation (Houthi-Saudi strikes, wider Iran war) and a softer dollar; gold and silver ores were among the top industry groups Friday. Lowest-cost senior producer.
positions.risks: Still 26% below its $255.24 March high; gold miners sell off fast if a hot CPI lifts real yields. Q3 report late October is outside the window.
positions.driver: Geopolitical hedge with improving momentum to balance the risk-on names.
